xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4961: Workspace disk floor is checked once per creation, so concurrent starts run the disk out (6 starts took 15 GB to 4.9 GB)

plan.title: Workspace disk floor is checked once per creation, so concurrent starts run the disk out (6 starts took 15 GB to 4.9 GB)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The code change spans four lint subsystems (src/lib, src/dashboard, tests/unit, tests/lib); the plan totals 28 files, the extra ones added by the round-1 critique (the real containerize route and its test). The remaining subsystems are documentation paths, which the projected-surface lint counts one subsystem per top-level doc path (docs/X.md, reference/X.mdx, sync-sources/skills, .overdeck/context). Splitting the docs into a sibling issue would ship the disk hold without its docs, which the PRD rule forbids, and splitting the code would ship a ledger nothing calls or a hold that one of the start paths (dashboard route, CLI in-process spawn, containerize route) never applies.

narratives.Problem: createWorkspace checks the 10 GiB disk floor once (src/lib/workspace-manager/create.ts line 203) and then writes the worktree and package install; the ~1.94 GB per-workspace Docker volume is written later by rebuildWorkspaceStack when the work agent starts. On 2026-11-03 six Flywheel starts each passed the check at 15-17 GB free and together took the disk to 4.9 GB, near the point where SQLite and git writes fail for every agent (PAN-1674).
narratives.Proposal: Add a cross-process reservation ledger to src/lib/disk-floor.ts: a disk-heavy phase is admitted only when available − in-flight reserved bytes − its own measured cost ≥ the floor, holds a reservation file while it runs, and releases it when it returns. Measure the per-project host and stack cost (git ls-tree blob sizes, unshared node_modules blocks, docker volume and unique image sizes) in src/lib/workspace/disk-cost.ts. Admit the host phase in createWorkspace and the stack phase in rebuildWorkspaceStack; re-check the plain floor before the package install and before every docker compose up. A work start whose stack needs a rebuild the disk cannot take answers HTTP 507 diskLow, which pan start prints and the finalize auto-handoff defers and retries. Planning already builds no stack; a test pins it and the docs explain where the observed stacks came from.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No disk check in evaluateSpawnGuardrails and no hold on a work start whose stack is already healthy
- No change to container-ops.ts start/restart/stop actions (they act on existing stacks)
- No change to the 10 GiB floor value, the disk-pressure patrol, or BuildKit pruning
- No refactor of src/lib/vault/file-lock.ts (imported as-is)
- No new HTTP route and no new UI; the PlanDialog Start Docker checkbox stays
- No attempt to subtract the part of an in-flight reservation already written to disk (over-counting is accepted)
- No support for Docker's data root on a different filesystem beyond documenting the assumption
- No raise of any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap
- No change to blockWork/escalation bookkeeping in spawn-prep.ts beyond the cli-start-disk-hold check; a rebuild refused by the ledger after the hold preview passed (a race) still surfaces as the generic stack-unhealthy error

autoDecisions.summary: Use a cross-process file ledger (~/.overdeck/disk-reservations/) serialized by withFileLock from src/lib/vault/file-lock.ts, not an in-process counter
autoDecisions.rationale: Workspace creation runs in the dashboard, the Deacon child process and CLI processes; serializing admission under one O_EXCL lock makes every admitted reservation visible to later admissions without ranking logic.

autoDecisions.summary: Two phases with separate measured costs (host: worktree + unshared node_modules; stack: compose volumes + unique image bytes), each released when its phase returns
autoDecisions.rationale: The phases run minutes apart in different code paths; after a phase returns its bytes are real and statfs sees them.

autoDecisions.summary: Measure directly and memoize 6 h; seed constants (0.5 GiB host, 2 GiB stack, rounded up from 2026-11-03 measurements) only for an unmeasurable component
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires a measured estimate; a statfs-delta measurement is contaminated by exactly the concurrent phases this issue is about, and du overstates hardlinked bun node_modules by ~2 GB.

autoDecisions.summary: Re-checks before install and compose are plain floor checks, not reservation-aware
autoDecisions.rationale: Subtracting reservations again would double-count the phase's own reservation and refuse already-admitted work.

autoDecisions.summary: Hold work starts only at the stack-health gate when a rebuild is needed (HTTP 507 diskLow), mapped to the retryable 'guardrails' skip reason
autoDecisions.rationale: A start whose stack is healthy adds no disk cost; mapping to guardrails reuses the existing deferred-handoff retry instead of failing the handoff.

autoDecisions.summary: Planning keeps building no Docker stack; add a pinning test and document the cause instead of changing planning
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified: PlanDialog defaults startDocker false, pan start sends none, the plan role skips stack health, and PAN-4840's stack was built by the finalize auto-handoff's work spawn (containers 15:56:31, agent 15:56:58, handoff spent 15:57:00).

autoDecisions.summary: Cover three Docker bring-up doors (createWorkspace startDocker, rebuildWorkspaceStack, WorkspaceService.containerize) and leave container-ops start/restart/stop out
autoDecisions.rationale: Only 'up -d --build' on a new or torn-down stack writes a new volume; start/restart reuse existing containers.

autoDecisions.summary: Set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of splitting into sibling issues
autoDecisions.rationale: The over-limit subsystem count comes from doc files counted one subsystem each; the code spans four subsystems and the slices are not independently useful.

items.title: Add the cross-process disk reservation ledger to disk-floor.ts

metadata.acJustification: Five ACs cover the five distinct ledger behaviors the critique required (N/k admission, release, reclaim, heartbeat, fail-closed); checkDiskFloor prefix and constant equality are covered by the retained existing tests.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-1 as revised after the round-1 critique: in src/lib/disk-floor.ts add DISK_LOW_HELD_PREFIX, DISK_RESERVATION_HEARTBEAT_MS (60 s), DISK_RESERVATION_STALE_MS (10 min), reserveDiskFloor and previewDiskFloor with DiskFloorLedgerDeps (read, ledgerDir default join(getOverdeckHome(),'disk-reservations'), withLock default withFileLock from ./vault/file-lock.js, isPidAlive via process.kill(pid,0) with EPERM=alive, now, setInterval). Admission runs under the lock: list *.json, delete entries whose pid is dead or whose file mtime is older than 10 min, refuse when available - reservedBytes - bytes < DISK_SAFETY_FLOOR_BYTES, else write <uuid>.json {pid,bytes,label,path,createdAt}, start an unref'd 60 s utimes heartbeat, and return an idempotent release that clears the heartbeat and deletes the file. statfs failure admits with a no-op release; ANY ledger failure (mkdir, listing, write, lock) refuses with the D-7 ledger-unavailable text (fail closed). Refusal text and the new checkDiskFloor text start with DISK_LOW_HELD_PREFIX; floor refusals contain '10.0 GiB'. Keep DISK_SAFETY_FLOOR_BYTES === DISK_PRUNE_TRIGGER_BYTES. Tests: mkdtemp ledger, injected read, in-process promise-chain mutex for withLock, injected isPidAlive/now, vi.useFakeTimers() for the heartbeat test; no real statfs.

items.title: Given read() returns 16 GiB and each call asks for 2 GiB, when 6 reserveDiskFloor calls run concurrently without releasing, then exactly 3 return ok: true and 3 return ok: false with an error that starts with 'Disk low — new workspace starts are held' and contains '10.0 GiB'

Given one admitted reservation is released, when a 7th reserveDiskFloor call runs at the same free space, then it returns ok: true and the released reservation file no longer exists in the ledger directory

Given a reservation file whose pid isPidAlive reports dead, or whose mtime is older than DISK_RESERVATION_STALE_MS while its pid is alive, when reserveDiskFloor runs, then that file is deleted and its bytes are not subtracted

Given fake timers and an admitted reservation whose holder stays alive, when 30 minutes are advanced, then a new reserveDiskFloor call still subtracts its bytes because the heartbeat renewed the file mtime

Given withLock throws, when 6 reserveDiskFloor calls run concurrently, then all 6 return ok: false with an error that starts with DISK_LOW_HELD_PREFIX and names the unavailable ledger; given read() throws instead, reserveDiskFloor returns ok: true

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-2 as revised after the round-1 critique: new src/lib/workspace/disk-cost.ts exporting DiskCostProject, WorkspaceDiskCost (stackSource 'measured'|'machine'|'seed'|'none'), estimateWorkspaceDiskCost, parseDockerSize, resetWorkspaceDiskCostMemo, invalidateWorkspaceDiskCostMemo, SEED_HOST_DISK_COST_BYTES (0.5 GiB), SEED_STACK_DISK_COST_BYTES (2 GiB), DISK_COST_MEMO_TTL_MS (6 h). NO shell anywhere: git and docker run through execFile argument vectors; unshared node_modules bytes come from an async Node readdir/lstat walk summing blocks*512 for files with nlink === 1, never following symlinks, at most 64 lstat calls in flight. hostBytes = ls-tree blob-size sum + unshared bytes of the newest finished sibling feature-* workspace's node_modules (else the primary checkout's). stackBytes (only with compose_template) = max over finished siblings of '<composeProject>_*' volume Size + '<composeProject>-*' image UniqueSize; with no sibling stack, max(largest compose-project volume group on the host, SEED_STACK) as 'machine'; docker failure -> seed. Any non-finite or negative parsed component counts as unmeasurable. Memoize the promise per project path; do not memoize rejections.

items.title: parseDockerSize returns 1938000000 for '1.938GB', 287300000 for '287.3MB', 512000 for '512kB' and 0 for '0B'

Given an injected docker df fixture with two sibling stacks of different volume sizes, estimateWorkspaceDiskCost returns stackBytes equal to the larger stack's volume Size plus image UniqueSize and stackSource 'measured'

Given no finished sibling stack but another compose project on the host with a 5 GB volume group, estimateWorkspaceDiskCost returns stackBytes 5000000000 with stackSource 'machine'; given the docker command rejects, it returns SEED_STACK_DISK_COST_BYTES with stackSource 'seed'

Given a temp dir holding one single-link file and one hardlinked pair, the default unshared-bytes walk returns only the single-link file's blocks; and a project path containing '"$(touch pwned)"' reaches exec as one argument-vector element with no 'pwned' file created

Given a memoized estimate younger than DISK_COST_MEMO_TTL_MS, when estimateWorkspaceDiskCost is called again for the same project path, then it returns the memoized value without invoking the injected exec; after invalidateWorkspaceDiskCostMemo(path) the next call invokes exec again
